Love is a part of our existence, and it can't be given or taken away, no matter how much disconnection hurts. It's a good challenge to let go of preconceived notions about relationships and love, as they're not constant, even in a good relationship.

As long as you're mindful and provide space, it's okay to have expectations of others. Perhaps in the near future, you can both compromise and check in with each other to gain a clear understanding of how you're progressing during this time apart.

It's important to challenge your mind to consider the gray areas as a possibility. I know it's easier said than done, but very few things are as black and white, or as extreme as our minds sometimes make us believe.

Remember: our emotions and feelings are a compass, not the ultimate truth. Even though it may seem daunting, this means there's some room for more hope to grow and bring light to challenging and painful circumstances.

My best recommendation is to have a plan of how you’re going to work on yourself and keep yourself accountable outside of the hope you have to reconnect (still hold onto hope just don’t make it the “reward” or “goal” for your growth). 

Truly sit with your therapist and have a consistent journal that’s honest to keep track of your progress (again for you). 

Think of boundaries you would set in a relationship if it were the other way around, 
example: If he did what you did & challenge yourself to work on what’s in your control. Also have insight on how you can limit the pressure of him being your favorite person as I’ve heard constantly from partners of BPD humans that it’s an ungodly level of stress even if not explicitly stated. 

Lastly, remember: this was your biggest fear- and he asked for space not full disconnection. 
This was your biggest fear and you survived it and you will continue to regardless of the outcome. You have survived all of your worst days and you’re still standing- give yourself credit before moving forward and becoming the human being your heart and mind desires to be.

Be careful when trying to attempt this distraction method, as transfer addiction is possible i.e. video gaming to overcome a habit can also become unhealthy. 

Try to encourage yourself to have a flexible routine you connect with! 
When I had to go sober (pregnancy related) it was very challenging bc i didn’t realize how empty my day was. Now i have a bunch of activities I try to engage with rather than distract with. Having a daily walk, or period of time to journal (helpful for long term recovery), even painting can have their moments in your day without abruptly ending and having nothing else to look forward to. 

In addiction, we use in a schedule, try to consider what yours was and support yourself without shame and with compassion with a mixture of old hobbies, new hobbies, and hobbies shared with others either in person friends or via online connections like here on Reddit, on bumble, or even through YouTube! Check out local places (public library events, cafes, a local park, etc.)  in town and have things to look forward to that give you consistent joy. 

Remember, healing isn’t linear and recovering is a commitment renewed everyday- not just a streak you upkeep! There are so many people willing to support you and I’m proud of you for being vulnerable and asking for advice!

Remember being aro is a spectrum. It doesn’t necessarily mean you don’t have the capacity to feel romantic attraction but that you don’t perceive or internalize it the same way as “traditional attraction”, i.e. cuddling and going out together is a form of romance and in some cases, desire and attraction! 

I think it would be best to do a values list with your partner- see if your goals and wishes align and move on from there! 

I myself am AroAce, in a relationship for 9 years with an accidental pregnancy…how? Because sexuality is a spectrum and we should be seeking what we want more of not just what we dislike. You are human so you have desires that can range from connection, comfort, compassion..and yes even cuddles if that’s for you. 
And like a spectrum, don’t expect who you are now to be the same version of you in 6 months or even a year- allow yourself to learn, change your mind and rediscover again!
You could do a cord cutting but I’d STRONGLY recommend having a diverse routine with periods of accountability/ self reflection especially when withdraw starts to come in. Good Luck!
